title: Optional Fields Without Temporaries
description: Build a config struct full of optional pointer fields using new(expr) instead of a pile of named temporaries, and prove the returned pointers do not alias the caller's values.
short_description: Delete the temporary variables and the ptr helper
learning_objectives: Use new with an expression instead of a type
Explain why new(expr) allocates rather than aliases
Keep nil meaningful as unset when zero is a real value
real_world_connection: Optional fields in API request types and config structs are almost always *int and *bool, and every codebase grows a ptr helper to populate them. This removes the helper.
requirements: NewConfig sets Retries, Debug and Label and leaves Timeout nil
Zero values must still produce non-nil pointers
Each call allocates its own memory
Bump returns a pointer to n+1 that does not alias the caller's variable
bonus_points: Write NewConfig the old way with three temporaries and compare the two
Try new(Config{Retries: new(3)}) and decide whether you prefer it to &Config{...}
